title: Optionally enable complex dtypes in OpInfo
author: beverlylytle
body: Currently, many tests configured by OpInfo have skipping complex-valued tensors hard-coded into the tests to speed up CI runs.  However, for some ops, eg imag, it makes no sense to skip complex dtypes.  We propose to add a flag to OpInfo instantiate_complex_tests that allows the op to opt in to testing on complex dtypes.  This flag would be checked instead of these existing checks.

title: [thunderfx] Problem with buffer updated during the forward - RuntimeError: Trying to backward through the graph a second time (or directly access saved tensors after they have already been freed).
author: kshitij12345
body: This was found while running BAAI/Bunny-v1_1-4B (see Repro with Model below) Model code which updates buffer during forward - https://huggingface.co/BAAI/Bunny-v1_1-4B/blob/2faf1780f240d4fc560d61142160a8562bfb6477/modeling_bunny_phi3.py#L1099-L1126 Minimal Repro import torch from thunder.dynamo import thunderfx import thunder  class Model(torch.nn.Module):     def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):         super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)         self.fc = torch.nn.Linear(2, 2)         self.register_buffer("buf", None, False)          # Ok if buffer is already populated.         # self.buf = torch.ones(2, 2, device=x.device)      def forward(self, x):         if self.buf is None:             self.buf = torch.randn(1, 2, device=x.device)         return self.fc(x) + self.buf      with torch.device("cuda"):     org_m = Model()     # m = org_m     m = thunderfx(org_m)     # m = thunder.jit(org_m)      x = torch.randn(2, 2)     m(x).sum().backward()      # With thunderfx, tensor([[1., 1.]], device='cuda:0', grad_fn=<ThunderFunctionBackward>)     # With eager, tensor([[1., 1.]], device='cuda:0')     # With thunder, None     print(org_m.buf)      m(x).sum().backward() With thunderfx path, the buffer that is saved has grad_fn=<ThunderFunctionBackward> and hence in the second iteration during backward, we incorrectly try to backward on this already freed part of the computation graph. Potential Solution: thunderfx's torch autograd integration should mark output from no_grad region or requires_grad=False (need to propagate this correctly see #1733 and #1768) as non-differentiable so that buffer won't hold onto the previously freed graph. For thunder.jit, it just ignores the buffer being updated and generates new value for self.buf for every invocation (will file a seperate issue) Repro with Model import torch import thunder from thunder.dynamo import thunderfx import transformers  with torch.device("cuda"):     model_name = "BAAI/Bunny-v1_1-4B"     config = transformers.AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True)     config.num_hidden_layers = 1     model = transformers.AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(                         config,                         torch_dtype=torch.float16,                         trust_remote_code=True,                         attn_implementation="eager",                     )      model = thunderfx(model)      ids = torch.randint(0, 10, (1, 128))     output = model(ids, labels=ids)     output.loss.backward()      ids = torch.randint(0, 10, (1, 128))     output = model(ids, labels=ids)     output.loss.backward() cc: @riccardofelluga

title: TransformerEngine : May fail to compute weight gradients if weight parameter has some operation before Linear
author: kshitij12345
body: Repro: import torch import thunder from thunder.executors.transformer_engineex import transformer_engine_ex  def fn(x, w):     with torch.autocast("cuda", torch.bfloat16):         return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, w)  with torch.device("cuda"):     x = torch.randn(32, 32, requires_grad=True)     w = torch.randn(32, 32, requires_grad=True)      # tfn = thunder.jit(fn)     tfn = thunder.jit(fn, executors=(transformer_engine_ex,))      o = tfn(x, w)     o.sum().backward()      print(w.grad)  # None with TE executor (otherwise there is some value).     thunder.last_traces(tfn)[0].save_trace("init_trc.py")     thunder.last_traces(tfn)[-1].save_trace("exec_trc.py") Initial Trace import thunder import thunder.core.dtypes as dtypes import thunder.core.prims as prims import thunder.torch as ltorch import torch from thunder.executors.torchex import no_autocast  @torch.no_grad() @no_autocast def computation(x, w):   # x: "cuda:0 f32[32, 32]"   # w: "cuda:0 f32[32, 32]"   ltorch.autocast_enter('cuda', torch.bfloat16, True, True)    # /home/kkalambarkar/lightning-thunder/scratchpad/test.py:317: 	        return torch.nn.functional.linear(x, w)   t4 = prims.convert_element_type(x, dtypes.bfloat16)  # t4: "cuda:0 bf16[32, 32]"   t5 = prims.convert_element_type(w, dtypes.bfloat16)  # t5: "cuda:0 bf16[32, 32]"   t6 = prims.linear(t4, t5, None)  # t6: "cuda:0 bf16[32, 32]"   ltorch.autocast_exit()   return (t6,) Problem: With #1838, we check the requires_grad on weight TensorProxy to determine if TransformerEngine should compute gradients for weight. But this fails when weight is not directly the input parameter but output of some operation (in above eg, output of conversion to bfloat16). As thunder does not properly propagate requires_grad (#1768), the TensorProxy after the conversion has requires_grad=False. NOTE: Directly using the requires_grad from the Runtime Tensor also won't work as the conversion happens under no_grad context, hence output will not have requires_grad=True. import torch  def fn(x, w):     with torch.no_grad():         x_bf16 = x.to(torch.bfloat16)         print(x_bf16.requires_grad)  # False         return x_bf16 @ x_bf16  x = torch.randn(16, 16, requires_grad=False, device="cuda")    w = torch.randn(16, 16, requires_grad=True, device="cuda")  fn(x, w) Thoughts on Solution: If instead of a single function which computes gradients for input, weight and bias (with FP8 GEMM), we could have a separate function (and symbol) to compute input, weight and bias gradients (need to check feasibility), then it should most likely work fine thanks to thunder's autograd routing the gradients correctly (and discarding computation when not required). cc: @IvanYashchuk Ref: NVBUG 5219259

title: implement decomposition for torch.linalg.multi_dot
author: t-vi
body: My immediate interest is in the context of #1956 where it is a rather special autoregistered backward implementation, but while multi_dot is not the most used PyTorch function, it may be worthwhile to implement a decomposition:  multi_dot reduces to a sequence of matmuls, some matmuls can be fused, when only some params use  gradients, a decomposed multi-dot will benefit from not needing derivatives.  The trick will be to re-implement the automatic optimal ordering: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/a40e876b08277795a6552cf5e77e8649237c6812/aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp#L861-L1097

title: Hybrid FSDP and DDP does not work (composable transforms)
author: t-vi
body: Currently FSDPTransform and DDPTransform are not composable:  FSDP will shard the tensors and make sure to set the distparallel_type=FULLY_SHARDED on the input tensor to the synchronize prim. DDP will then come and produce the FSDP synchronize input tensor ("wrapping" the FSDP model in DDP), but this looses the distparallel_type.  DTensor solves this by providing a "chain" of distributed in the placement= list. I would change the synchronize prim to take the distparallel_type as an argument rather than read it from the proxy. cc @crcrpar @ali-alshaar7

body: thunder.examine.examine currently needs to be given an unmodified function. If you pass in a non-working jitted function (which you are likely to have when using examine), it claims that the "unmodified function" is not working, which is misleading. Example: import torch import thunder import thunder.examine  def fn(x):     x[0].zero_()  jfn = thunder.jit(fn) x = torch.ones(2, 2) thunder.examine.examine(jfn, x) We could either grab the original function from the compile data or error out. cc @Borda @mruberry

title: [profile-guided optimization] The input tensor values are lost for the FX subgraphs
author: kiya00
body: 🐛 Bug In profile-guided optimization, we collect all FX graphs and benchmark each one to choose the fastest backend. This process requires actually running each graph. Currently, input tensors are randomly generated based on metadata extracted from placeholder Node in the GraphModule, which contains min/max if possible. The input to each GraphModule is typically available via either node.meta["example_value"] or node.meta["grapharg"].example: example_value holds a FakeTensor used for shape/type tracing. grapharg.example is a weak reference to the original input tensor, which contains value range info (e.g. min/max). In the specific case below, we only have access to the example_value (the FakeTensor), so the generated random tensor lacks value range constraints — which can lead to CUDA errors during execution. To Reproduce from transformers import AutoConfig import torch from torch.testing import make_tensor from functools import partial  config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained("microsoft/Phi-3.5-mini-instruct") batch_size = 1 seq_length = 256 shape = (batch_size, seq_length)  from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM  with torch.device("cuda"):     model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(config, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)     model.requires_grad_(True)     make = partial(         make_tensor,         low=0,         high=config.vocab_size,         device="cuda",         dtype=torch.int64,         requires_grad=False,     )     a = make(shape)     inputs = {"input_ids": a, "labels": a}  from thunder.dynamo.compiler import thunder_profile, thunder_optimize pmodel = thunder_profile(model) pmodel(**inputs) pmodel(**inputs) optmodel = thunder_optimize(pmodel) optmodel(**inputs) it failed at submod_2 > /wayan/lightning-thunder/thunder/dynamo/utils.py(888)get_timing() -> print(f"Error running benchmark {compile_fn.name}: {e}") (Pdb) l 883         def get_timing(compile_fn, timer_fn): 884             try: 885                 measurement = report.run_benchmark(compile_fn, timer_fn, reset_torch_dynamo=False) 886             except Exception as e: 887                 import pdb; pdb.set_trace() 888  ->             print(f"Error running benchmark {compile_fn.name}: {e}") 889                 return float("inf") 890             return sum(m.median for m in measurement if m is not None) GraphModule(   (submod_0): GraphModule()   (submod_1): GraphModule()   (submod_2): GraphModule() )  submod_2 has the op loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits_2, shift_labels_2, ignore_index = -100, reduction = 'mean'); which requires each element in shift_labels_2 between 0 and C, but currently we have no mechanism to infer the value range of shift_labels_2, since it is an intermediate tensor in the original full graph. Note that there's an inconsistency in how invalid inputs to cross_entropy are handled between eager mode and torch.compile. import torch from torch import device def forward(labels_1, logits_1):     getitem_1 = labels_1[(Ellipsis, slice(1, None, None))];  labels_1 = None     shift_labels = getitem_1.contiguous();  getitem_1 = None     logits_2 = logits_1.view(-1, 32064);  logits_1 = None     shift_labels_1 = shift_labels.view(-1);  shift_labels = None     shift_labels_2 = shift_labels_1.to(device(type='cuda', index=0));  shift_labels_1 = None     loss = torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(logits_2, shift_labels_2, ignore_index = -100, reduction = 'mean');  logits_2 = shift_labels_2 = None     return loss # the labels_1 is invalid, random from -9 to 9 sub_inputs = [torch.testing.make_tensor((1, 1025), dtype=torch.int64,  device='cuda:0', requires_grad=False, low=-9, high=9,), torch.testing.make_tensor((1, 1024, 32064), dtype=torch.float32,  device='cuda:0', requires_grad=True, low=-9.0, high=8.999998092651367,),]  import thunder print(torch.compile(forward)(*sub_inputs)) print(thunder.jit(forward)(*sub_inputs)) # fails randomly and the error can be caught with try-except, but the process cannot recover. forward(*sub_inputs) # fails and crashes immediately cc: @mruberry

title: [profile-guided optimization] The input tensors for the subgraph are newly allocated each time, which leads to OOM, whereas ThunderFX works.
author: kiya00
body: Note: If you have a model or program that is not supported yet but should be, please use the program coverage template. 🐛 Bug In profile-guided optimization, we collect subgraphs and run each one on different backends to select the fastest. However, the inputs to each subgraph are newly allocated on every run, which leads to additional memory usage. As a result, profile-guided optimization may run out of memory (OOM), while thunderfx handles the same workload without issue. Currently, the OOM occurs during benchmarking and is caught via exception handling, after which the default Thunder backend is selected. A potential improvement is to distinguish whether a subgraph input corresponds to the model input or an intermediate tensor. We can then restrict new allocations to only those inputs that are intermediate tensors, reducing unnecessary memory overhead. To Reproduce import torch from thunder.dynamo import thunderfx   from litgpt import Config, GPT from functools import partial from torch.testing import make_tensor  cfg = Config.from_name("Llama-3-8B")  cfg.n_layer = 10 cfg.block_size = 1024 batch_dim = 4  torch.set_default_dtype(torch.bfloat16) make = partial(make_tensor, low=0, high=255, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)  with torch.device("cuda"):     model = GPT(cfg)     shape = (batch_dim, cfg.block_size)     x = make(shape)  # works fine # thunderfx_model = thunderfx(model) # thunderfx_model(x)  from thunder.dynamo.compiler import thunder_profile, thunder_optimize  pmodel = thunder_profile(model)  pmodel(x) pmodel(x) # OOM when running the benchmark optmodel = thunder_optimize(pmodel) optmodel(x) RTX 6000 50G

title: [ThunderFX] RuntimeError: Advanced indexing currently only supports zero or one-dimensional integer tensors, but found a tensor with dtype thunder.dtypes.bool8 and 3 dimensions
author: kiya00
body: Note: If you have a model or program that is not supported yet but should be, please use the program coverage template. 🐛 Bug originated from the nvbug found when running nemo model SparseLLM/prosparse-llama-2-7b import torch import thunder from thunder.dynamo import thunderfx  def fn(x, idx, val):     x = x.clone()     x[idx] = val     return x  requires_grad=True #False  # only fails with `requires_grad=True`. x = torch.randn(1, 128, 11008, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=requires_grad) idx = torch.rand(1, 128, 11008) > 0.5 nz = torch.count_nonzero(idx) val = torch.randn(nz, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=requires_grad)  # fails with "RuntimeError: Advanced indexing currently only supports zero or one-dimensional integer tensors, but found a tensor with dtype thunder.dtypes.bool8 and 3 dimensions" thunder.jit(fn)(x, idx, val)   # thunderfx(fn)(x, idx, val)  The issue arises because the backward of setitem internally uses getitem, and in this case, the index for getitem is a boolean tensor. Currently, Thunder has limitations handling operators that depend on the runtime values of tensors. As @kshitij12345 mentioned in the nvbug: ThunderFX includes a code path to determine if an operation will fail for a given input (based on metadata) and provides a fallback mechanism in such cases (see here). However, in this scenario, the failure arises due to the use of indexing during the backward pass, which ThunderFX is unable to detect. One potential solution will be to also run backward in ThunderFX to determine if the fallback should be triggered.

title: Can JIT support a mode that skips cache lookup and prologue checks?
author: kiya00
body: 🚀 Feature Background: I'm investigating profile-guided optimization in ThunderFX. The idea is to separate the process into different phases: A profiling phase, where we gather statistics such as FX graphs and input metadata per graph. An optimization phase, where we pre-run each FX graph on different backends and select the fastest one. The actual execution, run the already optimized graphs This separation gives us the opportunity to determine in advance whether a given static graph can result in a cache hit, bypassing prologue checks. To further reduce Thunder compilation time, I'm exploring whether JIT could offer a mode that combines the "same input" cache behavior and skipping prologue checks. Currently, it seems the "same input" cache mode is not yet supported. import torch import thunder def model(x, y):     return x+y*y  a = torch.randn((2,2),device='cuda',requires_grad=True) b = torch.randn((2,2),device='cuda',requires_grad=True)  compiled_model = thunder.jit(model, cache="same input") compiled_model(a,b)  File "/wayan/lightning-thunder/thunder/core/jit_ext.py", line 2025, in thunder_general_jit     raise NotImplementedError(f"cache option {co.name} is not supported") NotImplementedError: cache option SAME_INPUT is not supported  cc: @mruberry

title: Increased memory usage for saved for backward with litgpt 0.5.5 compared to 0.5.4
author: IvanYashchuk
body: 🐛 Bug The benchmark_litgpt.py script demonstrates a consistent increase in GPU memory usage when using litgpt==0.5.5 compared to litgpt==0.5.4 (and litgpt==0.4.11). This behavior is observed for the CodeLlama-34b-hf model across different layer configurations (n_layer=2, n_layer=5) when compiled with Thunder. Steps to Reproduce (to observe memory increase)  Install litgpt==0.5.4:  pip install --no-deps litgpt==0.5.4  Run the benchmark with a reduced configuration to fit on 1 GPU, e.g., n_layer=5:  python thunder/benchmarks/benchmark_litgpt.py --max_iters 6 --warmup_iters 3 --model_name CodeLlama-34b-hf --compile thunder --n_layer 5  Note the "Memory used", "Saved for backward size", and "Saved for backward number of tensors" from the output. Install litgpt==0.5.5:  pip install --no-deps litgpt==0.5.5  Run the benchmark with the same configuration (n_layer=5):  python thunder/benchmarks/benchmark_litgpt.py --max_iters 6 --warmup_iters 3 --model_name CodeLlama-34b-hf --compile thunder --n_layer 5 Observed Behavior (Memory Increase)   n_layer=2:  litgpt 0.4.11: Memory used: 26.20 GB, Saved for backward: 13172.52 MiB, Tensors: 55 litgpt 0.5.4: Memory used: 26.20 GB, Saved for backward: 13172.52 MiB, Tensors: 55 litgpt 0.5.5: Memory used: 26.94 GB, Saved for backward: 13300.52 MiB, Tensors: 59 Difference (0.5.5 vs 0.5.4): +0.74 GB Used, +128 MiB Saved for backward, +4 Tensors saved    n_layer=5:  litgpt 0.5.4: Memory used: 54.02 GB, Saved for backward: 31784.98 MiB, Tensors: 127 litgpt 0.5.5: Memory used: 55.87 GB, Saved for backward: 32104.98 MiB, Tensors: 137 Difference (0.5.5 vs 0.5.4): +1.85 GB Used, +320 MiB Saved for backward, +10 Tensors saved    Impact  The increased memory footprint with litgpt 0.5.5 (when used with Thunder) can reduce the maximum feasible model size (e.g., number of layers, sequence length) or batch size that can be run on memory-constrained hardware compared to litgpt 0.5.4. This could lead to unexpected OOM errors for users upgrading their litgpt version while using Thunder for models that were previously operating close to the GPU memory limit. It may negate some performance benefits if users are forced to use smaller configurations due to this increased memory pressure. The effect is seen in the internal benchmarks where workloads previously passing on H100 now fail on B200 (which has more available memory)  Expected behavior For the same model configuration (e.g., CodeLlama-34b-hf, n_layer=5) and compiler (thunder), minor patch version updates of litgpt (like 0.5.4 to 0.5.5) should not lead to a significant increase in "Memory used" or "Saved for backward size", unless this increase is an intentional and documented change in litgpt or Thunder that provides a clear trade-off. Ideally, memory efficiency for activations should remain stable or improve. cc @crcrpar @lantiga, @t-vi

title: support torch.full with (scalar/1 element) tensor as value
author: t-vi
body: 🚀 Model / language coverage We currently only accept numbers as value in full. Pitch Apparently mask = torch.full((tgt_len, tgt_len), torch.tensor(torch.finfo(dtype).min, device=device), device=device) and is a pattern sometimes found in actual code. We could support this by mapping full with a single element tensor argument to .expand(shape).clone().to(...). Minimal Repro import torch, thunder def fn(a):    return torch.full((2,), a)  a = torch.tensor(1.0, dtype=torch.float64) print(fn(a))   # tensor([1., 1.]) jfn = thunder.jit(fn) jfn(a)  # exception (not the nicest error message, either): ValueError: Trying to extract a dtype from a non-numbertype object thunder.dtypes.float64! Note that the dtype is not the original dtype, but roundtripped through dtype->python-type->dtype (unless dtype is specified). title: Autodiff does not place recomputation in the correct order
author: riccardofelluga
body: 🐛 Bug While debugging TEv2 checkpointing I've noticed that some symbols are placed in the wrong order and proxies are used before they are called To Reproduce   executor for repro  from functools import partial  import torch import torch.utils.checkpoint  from thunder.core.prims import get_grad, put_grad from thunder.core.proxies import TensorProxy from thunder.extend import OperatorExecutor, register_executor import thunder.torch as ltorch  repro_ex = OperatorExecutor("repro_ex") register_executor(repro_ex)   def _pass_token_meta(tokens):     return (*(TensorProxy(like=token) for token in tokens),)   def _pass_token_impl(tokens):     return tokens   _pass_token = repro_ex.register_operator("pass_token", meta=_pass_token_meta, fn=_pass_token_impl)   def exec_transform(a, w, bias):     primal, _ = _pass_token((a, w))     return primal   def grad_transform(a, w, bias):     aw, bw = _pass_token((a, w))     primal, cd = _pass_token((bw, aw))     grad_out = get_grad(primal)     grad_a, grad_w, _ = _pass_token((grad_out, cd, aw))     put_grad(a, grad_a)     put_grad(w, grad_w)     return primal   repro_ex.register_implementation(     ltorch.linear,     checker=lambda a, w, bias: True,     execution_transform=exec_transform,     grad_transform=grad_transform, )  checkpoint_fn = partial(torch.utils.checkpoint.checkpoint, use_reentrant=False)   def fn(a, w0, w1):     b = checkpoint_fn(torch.nn.functional.linear, a, w0)     return torch.nn.functional.linear(b, w1)   x = torch.randn((16, 16), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True) w0 = torch.randn((16, 16), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True) w1 = torch.randn((16, 16), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)   from thunder.dynamo import thunderfx  jf = thunderfx(fn, executors=[repro_ex]) out = jf(x, w0, w1) print(jf.last_backward_traces[-1])  Produces the following trace where bw_t4 is used before it is created def backward_fn(saved_for_backward, cotangents):   # saved_for_backward: "Collection"   # cotangents: "Collection"   C0, _, = saved_for_backward   # C0: "Collection"   # None   clear_mutable_collection(saved_for_backward)   del saved_for_backward   t18, = cotangents   # t18: "cuda:0 f32[16, 16]"   clear_mutable_collection(cotangents)   del cotangents   t17, t14, l_a_, l_w0_, = C0   # t17: "cuda:0 f32[16, 16]"   # t14: "cuda:0 f32[16, 16]"   # l_a_: "cuda:0 f32[16, 16]"   # l_w0_: "cuda:0 f32[16, 16]"   clear_mutable_collection(C0)   del C0   (t19, t20, _) = dummy_pass_token((t18, t17, t14))   del t18, t17, t14   (_, bw_t7) = dummy_pass_token1((bw_t5, bw_t4))   del bw_t5   (bw_t4, _) = dummy_pass_token((l_a_, l_w0_))   del l_a_, l_w0_   (t9, t10, _) = dummy_pass_token((t19, bw_t7, bw_t4))   del t19, bw_t7, bw_t4   return (t9, t10, t20) Analysis For what I've understood the main problem lies here                lightning-thunder/thunder/transforms/autodiff.py                    Line 383       in       addb703                                                 for n in reversed(backward_part_bsym.flat_proxy_args):                     where we use the order the args appears in the boundsymbol to "decide" the insertion order. title: Wrong dtype for randint
author: beverlylytle
body: The operator randint in PyTorch returns int64 when no dtype is specified.  However when randint is Thunder-jitted, it returns float32.  The following example shows where this inconsistency between PyTorch and Thunder can result in an error. import thunder import torch   def f(x, y):     x.scatter_add_(index=torch.randint(0, 1, x.shape), src=y, dim=-1)     return x  x = torch.randn(2, 3) y = torch.randn(2, 3)  x_ = x.clone().detach() y_ = y.clone().detach()  z_ = f(x_, y_)  # this is fine.  jf = thunder.jit(f) z = jf(x, y)  # this throws an error `RuntimeError: index dtype=thunder.dtypes.float32 was not an integer dtype`

title: Support loading Transformer Engine FP8 checkpoints and compiling with the TE executor?
author: ultranationalism
body: 🚀 Feature Teach thunder.jit to parse FP8 scaling metadata from Transformer Engine & TensorRT-ModelOpt checkpoints. Motivation I have FP8-trained checkpoints produced by Transformer Engine native path:  Keys: layer.weight (E4M3), layer._extra_state  TensorRT-ModelOpt path:  Keys: layer.weight (E4M3), layer._amax  Thunder today only understands plain PyTorch tensors; it will happily load the files but ignores _extra_state / _amax, so the weights are treated as raw bf16/fp32 and the TE executor never receives the pre-computed scaling factors. As a result I must re-run calibration or stay in pure-TE inference, losing Thunder’s graph optimizations. Pitch Extend Thunder’s TE executor so that model.load_state_dict(torch.load('ckpt.pt'), strict=False) thunder.jit(model, executors=["transformer_engine_ex"]) recognises and imports  _extra_state _amax  and re-uses these values instead of re-collecting them during the delayed-scaling warm-up window. This would allow zero-copy loading of FP8 checkpoints while still utilising Thunder’s fusion pipeline.

title: Revert new primitive for grad bug fix; Apply localized solution for division output type consistency in _div_prim_grad
author: IvanYashchuk
body: 🐛 Bug Recently a problem was discovered preventing Thunder to execute one of the Hugging Face transformers model implementations (#2599). A fix for #2599 involved introducing a new primitive as suggested in #2599 (comment). It was implemented in #2626 and now merged. I don't think creating new primitives for bugs in grad definitions is the correct approach. Let's revert changes introduced in #2626 (80461ba) and add a proper localized fix in                lightning-thunder/thunder/core/transforms.py                   Lines 1137 to 1139       in       e30133a                                                 # NOTE The following grad definition relies on the fact that only inexact dtypes are differentiable,                                           #   and torch's true division operator and the division primitive agree on those types                                           def _div_prim_grad(a: Number | TensorProxy, b: Number | TensorProxy, /) -> Number | TensorProxy:                     As written in the note the implementation assumes that only inexact types would be passed to _div_prim_grad which is clearly not the case in reality. The problem is that Tensor[int32] / Tensor[int32] produces a float Tensor. So the fix is most likely is to replace / operator with prims.div. Since this _div_prim_grad implementation is registered for prims.div it should handle all inputs that prims.div handles and do not modify data type of the output. Minimal test case that should work to resolve bug observed in #2599. import torch, thunder  def fn(a, b, c):     indices = torch.div(a, b, rounding_mode="trunc")     return c[indices]  jfn = thunder.jit(fn) a = torch.randint(1, 5, (5,)) b = torch.ones(5, dtype=torch.int32) c = torch.randn(5, 5, requires_grad=True) print(fn(a, b, c)) print(jfn(a, b, c))
